    Infinite ray chains and the finite-state bound #

    Encode the alternating chains of BGRS 1.9 as walks on the finite type of nonzero category morphisms. A repeated state pumps to an infinite periodic chain. Consequently, absence of infinite chains supplies the common finite bound used by efficient-tackle selection.

                        theorem LargeIndecomposable.not_rayPeriodTwoCrown {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasNoInfiniteRayChain C] {X Y : C} (rho₀ : NonzeroHom X X) (sigma₀ : NonzeroHom Y X) (rho₁ : NonzeroHom Y Y) (sigma₁ : NonzeroHom X Y) (hpeak₀ : RayTargetIncomparable rho₀ sigma₀) (hvalley₀ : RaySourceIncomparable sigma₀ rho₁) (hpeak₁ : RayTargetIncomparable rho₁ sigma₁) (hvalley₁ : RaySourceIncomparable sigma₁ rho₀) :
                        False

                        Four nonzero morphisms alternating around two objects cannot form a period-two crown in a category with no infinite ray chains. This is the literal A~(rho₀, sigma₀, rho₁, sigma₁) obstruction used in Bongartz's dumb-bell argument; unlike RayClosedChain, it intentionally allows period two.
